thread.title: Wisconsin Graduate Student Eliotte Heinz Found Dead in Mississippi River After Disappearance
thread.title_full: Wisconsin Graduate Student Eliotte Heinz Found Dead in Mississippi River After Disappearance

author: Rudy Blalock
title: Wisconsin Graduate Student Eliotte Heinz Found Dead in Mississippi River After Disappearance
text:
The body of a missing 22-year-old graduate student was found Wednesday morning in the Mississippi River near Brownsville, Minnesota, ending a three-day search to its end. The student had vanished from the La Crosse riverfront early Sunday.
Last Seen Near Waterfront
Eliotte Heinz was last seen at around 3:22 a.m. Sunday, July 20, walking south on the 500 block of Front Street South in La Crosse, wearing a white T-shirt and jean shorts, according to the La Crosse Police Department’s initial July 20news release.At that time, authorities described Heinz as 5-foot-4, weighing 120 pounds, with blonde hair and blue eyes. Multiple attempts by family, friends, and police failed to find any trace of her.
Community Launches Search Efforts
Volunteers gathered at Viterbo University’s School of Nursing throughout Monday and Tuesday to coordinate search parties, the university said on itsFacebook page.The school served as a hub for the family and volunteers, distributing flyers and collecting donations of food, water, and supplies to support those searching for Heinz.
Viterbo University also called on area residents to review home security footage between 2 to 6 a.m. on July 20 in hopes that even small details could help. “Every share, every prayer, and every helping hand matters,” the school wrote in a post.
Body Found in Mississippi River
At 10:28 a.m. Wednesday, July 23, the La Crosse Police Department was notified by the Houston County Sheriff’s Department that a body had been found in the Mississippi River near Brownsville.In a subsequent
news release, the La Crosse Police confirmed that the body recovered was that of Eliotte Heinz, bringing the search to a heartbreaking end.Officers said the investigation is ongoing and that an autopsy will be conducted to determine the official cause of death.
“This was not the outcome we had hoped for throughout this search,” said La Crosse Police Chief Shawn Kudron. “Our thoughts are with Eliotte’s family, friends and all those who knew Eliotte. We are grateful for the outpouring of support from so many within the La Crosse community, the State of Wisconsin and nationally to locate Eliotte”.
Reactions and Community Support
In a statement posted on social media, Viterbo University wrote, “We are heartbroken by this loss and extend our deepest sympathies to her family and friends.”University President Dr. Rick Trietley said, “There are no words that can ease the pain of losing someone so young, with so much life ahead of her. Our hearts go out to Eliotte’s family. We hold them in our prayers and stand with them in their grief.”
The university plans to hold a memorial service in Heinz’s honor this fall, in coordination with her family, once students return to campus.
The Heinz family, through Viterbo University, conveyed gratitude for the “overwhelming” outpouring of support, kindness, and donations during the search in a
